chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Khalid ibn Jarir al-Bajali from Abu al-Rabii from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who managed the wealth of an orphan and borrowed something from it. He said: 'Indeed, Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them) used to borrow from the wealth of orphans who were under his guardianship, so there is no harm in that.'
ai.seo_question: Can a guardian borrow from an orphan's money?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the permissibility of a guardian borrowing from an orphan's estate, explicitly validating the practice of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS). In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a key precedent for financial flexibility, provided the guardian acts with integrity and does not exploit the orphan's assets, distinguishing it from mere consumption. The hadith underscores the principle that borrowing is permissible unless it leads to detriment, reflecting the pragmatic approach of the Imams in managing waqf and personal finances.
